findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at module import, not per instance
findings.body: In the `AssignmentSource` dataclass, `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` executes `timezone.now()` a single time when the class body is evaluated (at module import). Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` — which is all of them, since `from_integration` and the test constructors never pass it — shares the timestamp of process startup/module import rather than the time the assignment actually originated. This stale value is then serialized into every `sync_assignee_outbound` Celery payload via `to_dict()`. The field's apparent purpose (recording when the assignment was queued) is therefore defeated, and any future consumer reading `queued` would get a wrong, potentially days-old value. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so the default is computed per instance.

findings.title: `from_dict` performs no type coercion/validation, so `queued` round-trips as a string through the task queue
findings.body: `to_dict()` emits `queued` as a `datetime`, but the dict crosses the Celery boundary as the `assignment_source_dict` kwarg, where Sentry's JSON-based task serialization converts datetimes to ISO-8601 strings. `from_dict` then blindly splats the payload into the constructor (`cls(**input_dict)`), and dataclasses do not enforce type annotations, so after every real round trip `queued` is a `str` in a `datetime`-typed field — the class invariant is silently broken (the eager test runner does not serialize kwargs, so the tests don't catch this). The same lack of validation means a wrong-typed `integration_id` (e.g. a string after a future serialization change) would construct successfully and then never equal `org_integration.integration_id` in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync`, failing open and re-opening the exact sync cycle this PR exists to prevent. `from_dict` should parse `queued` back into a datetime (or the field should be dropped) and coerce/validate `integration_id`.

findings.title: No coverage that a different integration still propagates, or that deassign with a matching source is suppressed
findings.body: The new tests cover only two cases: no `assignment_source` (outbound sync proceeds) and a matching `assignment_source` on assign (outbound sync suppressed). The explicitly stated design goal — 'This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward' — is untested: nothing sets up external issues on two different integrations and asserts that an assignment sourced from integration A still triggers outbound sync to integration B. Additionally, the deassign path that now threads `assignment_source` (inbound webhook deassign → `GroupAssignee.objects.deassign(..., assignment_source=...)` → `sync_group_assignee_outbound`) has no test verifying that a matching source suppresses the outbound deassign to the originating integration. A regression in either direction (over-suppressing legitimate cross-integration syncs, or failing to suppress deassign echoes) would not be caught by this suite.
